text.p: Restaurant chain operator Shoney's Inc amended its bylaws to clarify the procedure for special shareholder meetings, but a dissident shareholder contends that it was done to entrench the company's management.
Shoney's spokesman Hank Dye said the changes in the company's by-laws are intended "to protect all shareholders rather than favor a single dissident shareholder."

"We are disappointed that Shoney's board and management would approve tactics which appear designed only to delay a Special Meeting of Shoney's shareholders and to entrench the current board and management," Raymond Schoenbaum said in a statement.
Schoenbaum and his mother, who hold a combined eight percent of the company's stock, formed the Shoney's Shareholders Committee to replace the company's board and top management.

Dye said the company, which generated $1.1 billion in revenues for the year ended October 1996, cannot specifically address Schoenbaum's claims until it makes its own filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

Shoney's changed the by-laws so Shoney's board sets the record date for special meetings, rather than the person requesting the meeting, and also changed who could serve as inspectors of election to now include Shoney's employees or officers.
A spokesman for Schoenbaum said the by-law changes alter the record date for the special meeting.
